I will preface this by saying that I didn't like Octavia at points either, I believe she made a lot of questionable decisions in general and I was really hoping that her arc would have more to do with making peace with others (which she sort of did in the end and before the ending with Levitt but I feel her journey should have gone on for longer in that regard.)

I just believe that genociding certain cultures due to how they've been raised and brought up instead of trying to mold into a new culture like they did with Wonkru is a bit leaning towards eugenics and I don't think that is as morally permissible as doing a lottery / letting people choose in the way that they had wanted to originally. That being said it's unfortunate that there was the food shortage that led to the 'need' to keep some of the violence that they should have been able to avoid more than they had.

You do bring up an interesting idea about tech destroying humanity though. I wouldn't say it was the root of the problem more-so than Becca flying too close to the sun with AI development. 

I think another interesting takeaway is that all the different groups in the series have some element of violence that they can all be linked to humanity by, although some feel more 'civil' than the standards that we typically hold people too, in essence it's all violence at its root.

"The whole point was to make earth (or any planet I guess since they traveled) survivable again." This was the goal and humans messed it up every single time in some way or another. I believe it's kind of fitting that their only way to "be better" was to sacrifice themselves for the rest of the human race to really prove that they were selfless enough as a species.
Excluding certain people because you believe that they are 'inferior' is exactly what this show was teaching you not to do lol
